name: Queen
hook: The London rock band behind 'Bohemian Rhapsody', whose bass-led 'Another One Bites the Dust' became Weird Al's first parody played live on the radio.

blurb.age13: Queen formed in London in 1970: Freddie Mercury singing and playing piano, Brian May on guitar, Roger Taylor on drums and, from 1971, John Deacon on bass. 'Bohemian Rhapsody' (1975) mixed rock, ballad and opera in one six-minute single. 'Another One Bites the Dust' (1980), built on Deacon's bass line, was a dance hit, and Michael Jackson was the one who urged them to release it as a single. Mercury died in 1991 from an illness caused by AIDS, the day after he told the public he had it. Their 1985 Live Aid set is often called one of the best live performances in rock.
blurb.adult: Formed in London in 1970, with Deacon joining in 1971, Queen recorded mainly for EMI and Elektra. 'A Night at the Opera' (1975) carried 'Bohemian Rhapsody'; 'The Game' (1980) carried Deacon's 'Another One Bites the Dust', which Michael Jackson urged them to release as a single after seeing them play, and their 1981 'Greatest Hits' became the UK's best-selling album. In 1984 they played nine shows at Sun City in apartheid South Africa, breaking the UN cultural boycott; the band said the audiences were integrated and that they gave to charity, and the shows drew wide criticism. Mercury was diagnosed with AIDS in 1987, announced it on 23 November 1991 and died the next day of bronchopneumonia. May and Taylor have continued as Queen, with Adam Lambert singing since 2011.
